title: Azure Files vs Blob Storage
description: Choose between Azure Files and Blob Storage for different data access patterns.

data.text: You need to migrate an on-premises application that uses SMB file shares to Azure. The app reads/writes files using standard file system APIs. Should you use Azure Files or Blob Storage?

Use **Azure Files** for SMB file share scenarios. It provides a fully managed SMB/NFS file share that can be mounted by VMs, App Service, and on-premises servers via Azure File Sync. Use **Blob Storage** for object/blob access patterns.

data.title: Azure CLI - Create Azure File Share
data.code:
# Create storage account
az storage account create \
  --name 'mystorage' \
  --resource-group 'rg-migration' \
  --sku 'Standard_LRS' \
  --kind 'StorageV2'

# Create file share
az storage share create \
  --account-name 'mystorage' \
  --name 'app-data' \
  --quota 1024

# Mount on VM (Linux)
mount -t cifs //mystorage.file.core.windows.net/app-data /mnt/appdata \
  -o vers=3.0,username=STORAGEACCOUNT,password=KEY,dir_mode=0777,file_mode=0777,serverino

data.text: **Azure Files** supports standard file system APIs (SMB/NFS), making it a 'lift-and-shift' solution. **Blob Storage** requires API changes. For legacy apps, Azure Files is the only option without code changes.
